For every a0>1, H^{a0}(I)=0, and dim_H(I)≤1.

patches.value: Fix a Euclidean space X, A⊆X and a real s; assume L1: s>0. Give X its Borel measurable structure. M001 with d=s identifies native μH[s](A) with the scale-cover formula. For positive s the empty-member summands vanish and each nonempty finite-diameter member has the ordinary real diameter power used in H. The supremum over extended positive scales equals the supremum over finite positive scales: the infimum at scale ∞ is no larger than the infimum at any finite scale. Countable covers are equivalent to sequences by enumeration and empty padding, with the same cost. Thus μH[s](A)=H^s(A). Restricting covers to smaller diameter bounds can only increase their infimum, so H^s_δ(A)≥H^s_r(A) whenever 0<δ≤r. The definition of H is its supremum over these contents; if that supremum is ∞, for every finite bound there is a scale exceeding the bound, and every smaller scale still exceeds it. Discharge L1 and universally generalize the arbitrary space, subset and exponent; F001 records this general statement with fresh bound names.

value.statement: For every Euclidean space X0, subset A0⊆X0 and real p0>0, μH[p0](A0)=H^{p0}(A0); for every 0<d0≤r0, H^{p0}_{d0}(A0)≥H^{p0}_{r0}(A0). Also H^{p0}(A0)=sup_{d0>0}H^{p0}_{d0}(A0), and H^{p0}(A0)=∞ implies these contents are unbounded as the positive scale tends to zero.

patches.value: For the arbitrary X,A,s assume L6: s>0. Under the additional antecedent L7: s<dim_H(A), apply M002 with the nonnegative real u=s; F001 converts its conclusion to H^s(A)=∞, and discharging L7 proves that implication. Under L8: dim_H(A)<s, M003 similarly gives H^s(A)=0; discharge L8. Under L9: H^s(A)=0, F001 gives μH[s](A)=0≠∞, so M004 gives dim_H(A)≤s; discharge L9. Under L10: H^s(A)=∞, F001 and M005 give s≤dim_H(A); discharge L10. Discharge L6 and universally quantify the arbitrary space, subset and exponent. Nonnegativity of dimension follows from its definition as a supremum in [0,∞].

value.statement: For every Euclidean space X0, A0⊆X0 and real p0>0: p0>dim_H(A0)⇒H^{p0}(A0)=0; p0<dim_H(A0)⇒H^{p0}(A0)=∞; H^{p0}(A0)=0⇒dim_H(A0)≤p0; H^{p0}(A0)=∞⇒dim_H(A0)≥p0. Also dim_H(A0)≥0 for every A0.

patches.value: For monotonicity fix B⊆X and temporarily assume L2: A⊆B. At every positive exponent s, any scale cover of B covers A, so its infimum bounds the content of A; taking suprema gives H^s(A)≤H^s(B). If dim_H(A)>dim_H(B), real order density supplies a finite positive exponent strictly between them (also when dim_H(A)=∞). F002 at that exponent and each set would give infinity on A and zero on B, contradicting the measure inequality. Hence dim_H(A)≤dim_H(B); discharge L2. For isometry let Y be Euclidean and assume L3: φ:A→Y preserves distances. Intersect the members of any cover of A with A and apply φ; they cover φ(A) with no greater diameters. Conversely inverse images in A of a cover of φ(A) cover A with no greater diameters, because φ preserves distance. Infima at each scale in both directions give equal contents at every positive exponent, and then H^s(φ(A))=H^s(A). If the dimensions differed, a positive finite exponent between them and F002 would again give zero on one side and infinity on the other. Discharge L3 and universally quantify X,A,B,Y,φ. The scale and critical assertions already hold universally by F001 and F002.
